hypothesis.statement: The whole remaining residual is ONE transposed callee-saved pair: ours `addi r30,r7,0` @0x24 (nd) and `lwz r31,548(r3)` @0x58 (d), against target `addi r31,r7,0` @0x24 and `lwz r30,548(r3)` @0x58; the downstream words at 0x94, 0xa0, 0xac, 0xb8, 0xe4 and 0xf0 are echoes of those two definitions. Declaration order predicts the TARGET assignment exactly (nd, d, yr, xr, e descending r31..r27), and the other four callee-saved values already land on target at their defining instructions - yr at `@0x50 lwz r29,536(r3)`, e at `@0x5c lwz r27,552(r3)`, xr at `@0x60 add r28,r6,r0` and the m parameter copy at `@0x20 addi r26,r5,0`, each byte-identical to the target's word at the same offset - so the allocator applies a fixed tie-break that promotes the memory-LOADED local d above the param-COPY local nd. The untried lever class is therefore neither declaration nor statement position but LIVE RANGE: nd's last use is 0xf0 and d's is 0x94, and in the target the LONGER-lived value takes r31 while in ours the shorter-lived one does. A construct that shortens nd's live range (or lengthens d's) without changing the instruction count is the next thing to try - for example sourcing the second MBFontMsgSetAlpha argument from a re-read rather than from the surviving copy.
